title: Why "the Way"?
question: When Jesus says no one comes to the Father except through Him, what does He mean by being the only way, truth, and life?
blurb: Jesus calls Himself the road to the Father, and the rest of Scripture shows us where that road leads.

title: Why "the LORD is my shepherd"?
question: If the LORD is my shepherd, what does He actually do for me that means I shall not want?
blurb: David calls God his shepherd and lacks nothing. Trace what a shepherd does to see what that promise holds.

title: Made in God's Image?
question: What does Scripture show is true of people because they bear the image of God?
blurb: One verse says we bear God's image - trace what Scripture reveals that means for every human life.

title: What Rest Does Jesus Give?
question: What is the weariness Jesus invites us to bring Him, and what kind of rest does He promise in return?
blurb: Jesus calls the weary and burdened to come to Him - and what He offers in return is more than a pause from work.

title: By His Wounds, Healed?
question: How can the suffering and wounds of one person bring peace and healing to others?
blurb: A wounded Servant takes the punishment we earned, so that His hurt becomes our healing and peace.

title: Good in All Things?
question: For whom, and toward what end, does God work all things together for good?
blurb: A promise with an address: trace who it's for and the purpose it's aiming at.

title: Who Is the Word?
question: Who is "the Word" who was with God and was God in the beginning?
blurb: One verse hides a Person in plain sight, present at creation, with God and yet God. Follow the trail Scripture leaves.

title: Peace Over Anxiety
question: What does God give in place of our anxiety, and how do we receive it?
blurb: Instead of worry, Paul points us to prayer—and to a peace that guards the heart beyond all understanding.

title: Who Is "I AM"?
question: When God names Himself "I AM," what is He revealing about who He is?
blurb: At a burning bush, God answers Moses with a name unlike any other - and it still echoes across all of Scripture.

title: Whose Understanding?
question: What does it look like to trust the LORD with all my heart instead of leaning on my own understanding?
blurb: A daily look at what it means to hand God the whole heart and let Him straighten the road ahead.

title: Why Did Jesus Weep?
question: If Jesus knew He was about to raise Lazarus, what moved Him to weep at the tomb?
blurb: The shortest verse in the Bible holds the deepest comfort: God in the flesh, weeping with those who grieve.

title: Plans to Give a Hope
question: What does God say His plans for His people are, and on what does He base that promise?
blurb: A famous promise spoken to exiles: the LORD knows His plans, and they are toward a future and a hope.

title: What Is Love Really Like?
question: What is the love that "never fails" actually like, as Scripture describes it?
blurb: Paul paints love not as a feeling but as patient, humble action - trace what it does and where it comes from.

title: The First Promise
question: In the curse on the serpent, what does God promise about the woman's seed and the enemy's defeat?
blurb: Spoken in Eden's darkest hour, the first hint of a coming Rescuer who will crush the serpent.

title: Seek First His Kingdom
question: What does Jesus mean by seeking the kingdom of God first, and what does He promise will follow?
blurb: One command reorders everything we chase: put God's kingdom first, and watch what He promises to add.

title: Can a Heart Be Clean Again?
question: When sin has stained the heart, what is David asking God to do that only God can do?
blurb: David doesn't ask to fix himself; he asks God to create something new in him. What is that prayer really after?

title: What Faith Really Is
question: If faith is being sure of what we cannot see, what does the rest of Scripture show that confidence resting on?
blurb: Hebrews calls faith assurance and certainty - let's trace how the Bible itself fills out what that means.

title: What Does God Require?
question: If God has shown us what is good, what are the three things He asks of us in return?
blurb: God strips it all down to three simple, weighty words: do justice, love mercy, walk humbly with Him.

title: How Did God Love Us?
question: What does God's love look like in action, and what does He give to those who believe?
blurb: One verse holds the heart of the gospel - trace how God's love gives, saves, and lasts forever.

title: But If Not
question: What kind of faith trusts God even when He might not rescue?
blurb: Three men face the furnace with a faith that bows to no idol, whether God delivers them or not.

title: Why Be Still?
question: What truth about God lets us stop striving and rest, even when nations rage and the earth shakes?
blurb: A command to be still in the middle of chaos - and the reason it's possible: God Himself.

title: How Does God Prove His Love?
question: When did God show His love for us, and what did it cost Him?
blurb: God didn't wait for us to clean up first. See the timing and the cost that proved His love.

title: Who Will Go?
question: What makes Isaiah ready to answer "Here am I; send me"?
blurb: A holy God asks who will go, and one cleansed man dares to volunteer. What got him there?

title: No More Tears?
question: What does God promise to remove forever, and what makes that promise certain?
blurb: A glimpse of the end God is writing: every tear wiped, death undone, and all things made new.

title: Who Will See God?
question: What is a "pure" heart, and how does that purity lead to seeing God?
blurb: A clean heart is promised the greatest sight of all - God Himself. What does that purity look like, and how is it received?

title: Where Courage Comes From
question: What reason does God give Joshua to be strong and courageous instead of afraid?
blurb: A command to be brave that rests not on Joshua's strength, but on one promise: God goes with him wherever he goes.

title: Be Transformed, Not Conformed
question: How does renewing the mind change us, and what does it let us discern?
blurb: One verse, two paths: drift with the world, or be made new from the inside out.

title: Fearfully and Wonderfully Made?
question: What does it tell me about God that He made me so carefully, and how should I respond?
blurb: The same God who knit you together knows you completely - and that truth turns wonder into worship.

title: A Time for Everything?
question: If God sets a season for every purpose, how should we live within His timing rather than our own?
blurb: Every season under heaven has its hour. Trace how Scripture frames God's timing and how we are to meet it.

title: Sent to Make Disciples
question: What is the church actually sent to do, and on whose authority?
blurb: Before He ascended, Jesus gave one marching order. See what He sent His followers to do, and why.

title: Go From Your Country
question: What is Abram asked to leave, and what is he promised instead?
blurb: One command, one promise, and a family that would bless every nation. Trace where the call leads.

title: Intended for Good
question: How can the same act be evil in one hand and good in another?
blurb: Joseph's brothers meant harm. Follow the thread from the pit to the palace and see what he concluded.

title: No Other Gods
question: Why does the first commandment come first?
blurb: Everything else in the Ten Commandments rests on this one. See what Scripture builds on top of it.

title: With All Your Heart
question: What does it look like to love God with everything you are?
blurb: Israel recited this daily, and Jesus called it the greatest commandment. Explore why.

title: Where You Go, I Will Go
question: What made Ruth stay when leaving would have been easier?
blurb: A foreign widow binds herself to a grieving mother-in-law, and ends up in the family line of a king.

title: The LORD Looks at the Heart
question: What does God see that people consistently miss?
blurb: Samuel was sure he'd found the king. Follow what Scripture says about how God actually measures a person.

title: If My People Humble Themselves
question: What does God ask of a people who have wandered?
blurb: Four verbs and a promise, spoken over a newly built temple. See where else they show up.

title: I Know My Redeemer Lives
question: What did Job still hold onto after losing everything?
blurb: From the ash heap, Job says something startling about the future. Follow where that hope goes.

title: A Lamp to My Feet
question: What kind of light does Scripture claim to give?
blurb: A lamp shows the next step, not the whole road. See how the Bible describes its own light.

title: Taste and See
question: Why does the psalmist say taste rather than think?
blurb: An invitation to find out for yourself. Trace what Scripture says God's goodness is actually like.

title: Guard Your Heart
question: Why is the heart the thing to guard above all else?
blurb: Proverbs says everything flows from one spring. See what Jesus said flows out of it.

title: They Will Soar on Wings
question: What does waiting on God have to do with strength?
blurb: Isaiah puts tired people next to an untiring God. Follow the comparison he's drawing.

title: A Heart of Flesh
question: What is God promising to replace, and with what?
blurb: Not a better effort but a new heart. See where else Scripture promises the same exchange.

title: The Righteous Will Live by Faith
question: Why do three New Testament writers all reach for this one line?
blurb: A single sentence from a minor prophet turns up at the heart of the New Testament. Follow it.

title: He Rejoices Over You
question: How does God feel about His people, in His own words?
blurb: A prophet of judgment ends with singing. See what Scripture says God delights in.

title: Ask, Seek, Knock
question: What is Jesus promising to the one who keeps asking?
blurb: Three verbs and a Father who answers. Explore what Scripture says about asking.

title: Not to Be Served
question: How does Jesus redefine greatness for His followers?
blurb: The disciples were arguing about rank. His answer turned the whole ladder upside down.

title: While He Was Still Far Off
question: Who moves first in the story of the lost son?
blurb: The son rehearses a speech. The father runs before he can finish it. Follow what happens next.

title: I Am the Vine
question: What does Jesus say fruit actually depends on?
blurb: Branches don't strain to produce grapes. See what Scripture says about staying connected.

title: They Devoted Themselves
question: What did the very first church actually do together?
blurb: Four habits, listed plainly. Trace what grew out of them in the verses that follow.

title: Confess and Believe
question: What does Paul say saving faith looks like from the outside?
blurb: A mouth and a heart, named together. See how the surrounding verses fill it out.

title: A Way of Escape
question: What does God promise about temptation, and what does He not promise?
blurb: Not the absence of pressure, but something else. Follow what Scripture says the way out is.

title: A New Creation
question: What exactly becomes new when someone is in Christ?
blurb: Paul says the old has gone. See what the surrounding verses say has arrived.

title: The Fruit of the Spirit
question: Why is it fruit that is grown, rather than rules that are kept?
blurb: Nine words describing a life. Explore what Scripture says produces them.

title: By Grace, Through Faith
question: If salvation is not earned, what is it for?
blurb: Paul rules out boasting in one breath and names a purpose in the next. Follow both.

title: God-Breathed
question: What does Scripture claim about where it came from and what it is for?
blurb: Paul makes two claims in one sentence: an origin and a use. Trace them both.

title: Living and Active
question: What is the word of God described as doing?
blurb: Not a text to be examined, but something that examines. See the images Scripture uses for itself.

title: Doers of the Word
question: What does James say happens when hearing never becomes doing?
blurb: A mirror, a forgetful glance, and a warning. Follow the picture James draws.

title: Cast Your Cares
question: What reason does Peter give for handing your worry over?
blurb: The instruction comes with a because. Trace what Scripture says about who is carrying it.

title: I Stand at the Door
question: Who is Jesus knocking for in this letter, and what is He asking?
blurb: A door, a knock, and a shared meal. See what Scripture says about who opens it.

title: The Blessing They Spoke
question: What is God promising when His name is spoken over His people?
blurb: The oldest blessing in Scripture, and the verses that fill in what it means.

title: Higher Than Ours
question: If God's thoughts are not our thoughts, how does Scripture say we respond?
blurb: A gap between His mind and ours — and four verses that sit in that gap.

title: Planted by the Water
question: What is the tree rooted in, and what makes it fruitful?
blurb: A picture of a rooted life. Trace where else Scripture plants that same tree.

title: A City on a Hill
question: If we are the light, whose light is it, and who is meant to see it?
blurb: Light given, light reflected. Follow the thread from Isaiah to the Sermon on the Mount.

title: Whatever You Do
question: What changes about ordinary work when it is done for the Lord?
blurb: Four verses about the daily, unglamorous work — and who it is really for.

title: He Loved First
question: Where does our love come from, and what does it look like once it arrives?
blurb: Love that starts somewhere else. See where John says it goes next.

title: Joy as Strength
question: How can joy be a source of strength rather than a result of it?
blurb: Said to a weeping crowd. Four more verses that put joy and strength together.

title: New Every Morning
question: What does Scripture say is renewed each day, and what stays the same?
blurb: Written in the ruins of a city. Sit with the verses that keep company with it.

title: Hearts Burning on the Road
question: What were they shown that made the Scriptures suddenly burn?
blurb: Two travellers, one stranger, and the whole of Scripture opened up.

title: God Will Provide the Lamb
question: Who does Scripture say the promised lamb turned out to be?
blurb: A father's answer on the mountain, and where the New Testament takes it.

title: The Gentle Whisper
question: Why was God in the whisper and not in the wind, earthquake, or fire?
blurb: A prophet at the end of himself, and the quiet that met him there.

title: Iron Sharpens Iron
question: What does Scripture say friends are actually for?
blurb: Sharpening takes friction. Four verses on the people who do it well.

title: No Longer I
question: What does Paul mean that he lives, yet not he?
blurb: An old life ended and a new one begun. Follow the idea across the letters.

title: He Emptied Himself
question: What did Christ let go of, and what does Paul ask us to do with that?
blurb: An early hymn about downward movement. See where else Scripture describes it.

title: Not by Might
question: If the work is not done by strength, how does Scripture say it gets done?
blurb: Said over a half-built temple. Four verses about small means and large outcomes.

title: You Will Be My Witnesses
question: What are the disciples given before they are sent, and what are they sent to say?
blurb: Power first, then going. Trace what the witnesses were actually witnesses of.

title: Mercy, Not Sacrifice
question: Why would God prefer mercy to the offerings He Himself commanded?
blurb: A line Jesus quoted twice. See what the prophets and the Gospels do with it.

title: Always, Continually, In Everything
question: How do rejoicing, prayer, and thanks belong together?
blurb: Three short commands in a row. Four verses that show what they look like lived out.

title: Let Justice Roll Down
question: What does God ask for when He turns down the worship being offered?
blurb: A prophet interrupts a festival. Follow justice through the Law, the Prophets, and James.

title: But Who Do You Say I Am?
question: Peter answers the question — where did his answer come from?
blurb: The question Jesus asks His friends directly. Sit with four other answers Scripture gives.

title: And I Was Not Aware
question: How often is God present somewhere before anyone notices?
blurb: Jacob wakes up on a stone pillow. Four verses about ground that turns out to be holy.
